correctness.rationale: The illumination event follows from necessary tip illumination plus positive spanning of tetrahedral directions. Twelve opposite-family spherical caps have distinct interiors exactly when 2 alpha <= arccos(-1/3), and each cross pair has center separation arccos(1/3). Gauss--Bonnet evaluates the lens area. The parabolic lens tangency calculation proves the 3/2 onset coefficient. Endpoint coverage and zero probability follow from the tetrahedral covering radius and lens tangency. Independently integrated lens areas, exact tetrahedral incidence checks, a high-precision asymptotic sequence and seeded randomized axes agree. No finite experiment is used as proof.

value.rationale: The joint hit probability for two antipodal spikes is a motivated geometric correlation that cannot be reconstructed from a one-tip marginal. It has an exact nontrivial radius window and a sharp finite critical cutoff despite existence of alternative four-beam solutions; the 3/2 onset quantifies the precise mechanism of random-method failure. The result is not an arbitrary parameter table or mere recomputation of a known one-cap probability.
